answer: A tight ring of 36 clones thus holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Because the crystal calculation reruns each epoch, the dune weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the wharf settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 56% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 35 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
